title: Not the wicked but the simple
source_text: Μετὰ ταῦτα τοσαῦθ᾿ ἡμᾶς αἰτιασάμενος θέλει ἐμφῆναι ὅτι καὶ ἕτερα ἔχων λέγειν παρασιωπᾷ αὐτά. ἔχει δ᾿ οὕτως αὐτοῦ ἡ λέξις· ταῦτα μὲν αἰτιῶμαι καὶ τὰ τοιαῦτα, ἵνα μὴ πάντ᾿ ἀπαριθμῶ, καί φημι πλημμελεῖν αὐτοὺς ἐπηρεάζοντας εἰς τὸν θεὸν, ἵνα πονηροὺς ἀνθρώπους ὑπάγωνται κούφαις ἐλπίσι καὶ παραπείσωσι καταφρονῆσαι τῶν κρειττόνων, ὡς, ἐὰν ἀπέχωνται αὐτῶν, ἄμεινον αὐτοῖς ἔσται. καὶ πρὸς ταῦτα δὲ λέγοιτ᾿ ἂν ἀπὸ τῆς περὶ τῶν προσερχομένων χριστιανισμῷ ἐνεργείας ὅτι οὐ πάνυ τι πονηροὶ ὑπάγονται τῷ λόγῳ ὅσον οἱ ἁπλούστεροι καὶ (ὡς ἂν οἱ πολλοὶ ὀνομάσαιεν) ἄκομψοι. οὗτοι γὰρ φόβῳ τῷ περὶ τῶν κολάσεων τῶν ἀπαγγελλομένων. κινοῦντι αὐτοὺς καὶ προτρέποντι ἐπὶ τὸ ἀπέχεσθαι τούτων, δι᾿ ἃ αἱ κολάσεις. πειρῶνται ἐπιδιδόναι ἑαυτοὺς τῇ κατὰ χριστιανισμὸν θεοσεβείᾳ· ἐπὶ τοσοῦτον ὑπὸ τοῦ λόγου κρατούμενοι, ὡς φόβῳ τῶν κατὰ τὸν λόγον ὀνομαζομένων αἰωνίων κολάσεων πάσης τῆς παρ᾿ ἀνθρώποις κατ᾿ αὐτῶν ἐπινοουμένης βασάνου καὶ μετὰ μυρίων πόνων θανάτου καταφρονεῖν· ὅπερ οὐδεὶς ἂν τῶν εὖ φρονούντων φήσαι πονηρῶν προαιρέσεων ἔργον εἶναι. πῶς δ᾿ ἀπὸ προαιρέσεως πονηρᾶς ἐγκράτεια καὶ σωφροσύνη ἀσκεῖται ἢ τὸ μεταδοτικὸν καὶ κοινωνικόν; ἀλλ᾿ οὐδ᾿ ὁ πρὸς τὸ θεῖον φόβος, ἐφ᾿ ὃν ὡς χρήσιμον τοῖς πολλοῖς παρακαλεῖ ὁ λόγος τοὺς μηδέπω δυναμένους τὸ δι᾿ αὑτὸ αἱρετὸν βλέπειν καὶ αἱρεῖσθαι αὐτὸ ὡς μέγιστον ἀγαθὸν καὶ ὑπὲρ πᾶσαν ἐπαγγελίαν· ἐξ ὧν οὐ τοῦτο τῷ κατὰ πονηρίαν αἱρουμένῳ ζῆν ἐγγενέσθαι πέφυκεν.
pass_a_gloss: After these, having accused (αἰτιάομαι) us of so many things, he wishes to make plain (ἐμφαίνω) that having other things to say he passes them over in silence (παρασιωπάω). His wording (λέξις) is thus: these things I accuse and such things, so as not to enumerate (ἀπαριθμέω) all, and I say they err (πλημμελέω) insulting (ἐπηρεάζω) against God, so that they may lead on (ὑπάγομαι) wicked (πονηροί) men with light/empty hopes (κοῦφαι ἐλπίδες) and persuade (παραπείθω) them to despise (καταφρονέω) the better things (κρείττονα), as, if they abstain (ἀπέχομαι) from them, it will be better for them. And to these it might be said from the working (ἐνέργεια) concerning those coming (προσέρχομαι) to Christianity, that not so much the wicked are led on by the word as the simpler (ἁπλούστεροι) and (as the many would name them) unrefined (ἄκομψοι). For these, by fear (φόβος) about the punishments (κολάσεις) announced (ἀπαγγέλλω), moving (κινέω) and urging (προτρέπω) them to abstain from those things on account of which are the punishments, try to give themselves (ἐπιδίδωμι ἑαυτούς) to the worship of God (θεοσέβεια) according to Christianity; being so far mastered (κρατέω) by the word, that by fear of what are named according to the word eternal punishments (αἰώνιοι κολάσεις) they despise every torture (βάσανος) devised (ἐπινοέω) against them among men and death with countless pains (μυρίοι πόνοι); which no one of those thinking well (εὖ φρονοῦντες) would say is the work of wicked choices. How from a wicked choice are self-control (ἐγκράτεια) and temperance/chastity (σωφροσύνη) practised (ἀσκέω), or sharing (τὸ μεταδοτικόν) and fellowship (τὸ κοινωνικόν)? But not even the fear toward the divine, to which as useful (χρήσιμος) to the many the word exhorts (παρακαλέω) those not yet able to see what is choiceworthy for its own sake and choose it as greatest good and above every promise (ἐπαγγελία); from which [things] this does not by nature (πέφυκεν) come to be in one choosing (αἱρέομαι) to live in wickedness (πονηρία).
pass_b_english: After charging us with so much, he wants to make it plain that he has other things he could say but passes them over in silence. His words run thus: “These things and the like I find fault with, so as not to list them all; and I say that they do wrong in insulting God, in order to lead on wicked men with empty hopes and persuade them to despise better things, on the ground that if they keep away from them it will be better for them.”

To this one might reply, from what actually happens among those who come to Christianity, that it is not so much the wicked who are led on by the word as the simpler sort and, as most people would call them, the unpolished. For these people, through fear of the punishments that are proclaimed, a fear which moves them and urges them to keep away from the things that bring punishment, try to give themselves to the worship of God that Christianity teaches. And the word so masters them that, through fear of what the word calls eternal punishments (Matthew 25:46), they despise every torment men devise against them, and death with countless pains. No one of sound mind would say that this is the work of wicked choices.

How can self-control and chastity, or generosity and readiness to share, be practised out of a wicked choice? Nor can the fear of God spring from such a choice, the fear to which the word, as something useful for the many, calls those who cannot yet see what is to be chosen for its own sake and choose it as the greatest good, above every promise. From all this it follows that such things do not by nature arise in one who chooses to live in wickedness.

choices.choice: Copy-text: staged source_3.json section 78 (Koetschau 3.78). Celsus's own words ('ταῦτα μὲν αἰτιῶμαι ... ἄμεινον αὐτοῖς ἔσται'), introduced by 'ἔχει δ᾿ οὕτως αὐτοῦ ἡ λέξις', are in double quotation marks. 'ἐπηρεάζοντας εἰς τὸν θεόν': Celsus means the supreme God, so capitalised. 'κούφαις ἐλπίσι' rendered 'empty hopes' throughout 78-80. 'αἰωνίων κολάσεων' named 'according to the word' points to Matthew 25:46 (κόλασιν αἰώνιον); cited inline. 'ὁ πρὸς τὸ θεῖον φόβος' (fear toward the divine) rendered 'the fear of God'. The final clause 'ἐξ ὧν οὐ τοῦτο τῷ κατὰ πονηρίαν αἱρουμένῳ ζῆν ἐγγενέσθαι πέφυκεν' is awkward (perhaps 'οὐδὲν τούτων'); rendered by sense, with 'ἐξ ὧν' as 'from all this it follows': such things do not by nature arise in one who chooses to live in wickedness — doubtful reading. The staged stops after 'ἀπαγγελλομένων.' and 'αἱ κολάσεις.' are punctuation noise.
In Celsus's quotation, 'do wrong and insult God' changed to 'do wrong in insulting God' (πλημμελεῖν ... ἐπηρεάζοντας: the participle gives the wrong done, not a second act)
'if they keep away from these things' changed to 'if they keep away from them' (αὐτῶν = the better things just named)
'it is not really the wicked who are led on ... so much as' changed to 'it is not so much the wicked who are led on ... as' (οὐ πάνυ τι ... ὅσον; removed the doubled qualifier)
Final clause now renders 'ἐξ ὧν' ('From all this it follows that ...'), which the first draft left out
Checked Matthew 25:46 (κόλασιν αἰώνιον), correct verse; Celsus's words kept apart from Origen's reply
